Thought: I need to analyze each statement about batrachotoxin and determine which one(s) are false.

Statement A: "Batrachotoxin is a steroid alkaloid found in the skin of poison dart frogs"
This is actually true. Batrachotoxin is indeed a steroidal alkaloid that is found in the skin secretions of certain poison dart frogs (genus Phyllobates) from Colombia.

Statement B: "it causes a blockade of Na+ channels and is therefore neurotoxic"
This statement is false. Batrachotoxin actually causes the opposite effect - it activates sodium channels by preventing them from closing, keeping them permanently open. This leads to continuous depolarization of nerve and muscle cells, which is why it's neurotoxic. It doesn't block Na+ channels, it keeps them open.

Statement C: "it is lethal only after oral ingestion"
This statement is also false. Batrachotoxin can be lethal through various routes of exposure, not just oral ingestion. It can enter the body through skin absorption, injection, or inhalation as well. Indigenous tribes use it on dart tips for hunting, which would involve the toxin entering the prey's bloodstream directly.

So statements B and C are false.
